rationale:
Evidence: iteration 7 is the best verified design (344.5). Its oval result was 17 of 20 finishes (progress 0.95, mean time 1.86 s). Its s-bend (progress 0.34) and slalom (progress 0.11) still leave the tape, with 1.15 and 1.25 line-loss events per run and steering oscillation of 0.22 and 0.14. Iteration 9 changed only kd (0.6 to 0.8) and reproduced iteration 7's scores to four decimals on every track, so kd does not appear to change the outcome, and the same happened for the kp and base_speed changes in iteration 6. The only verified gain is the iteration-7 plant change.

Changes: (1) Restore kd to 0.6, the verified value, so the draft is not confounded by the iteration-9 change. (2) Keep the full iteration-7 geometry: 8 mm sensors at x = -0.016 to +0.016 m (8 mm spacing), y = 0.06 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg. (3) Lower base_speed from 1.3 to 1.2 m/s. The s-bend and slalom failures are tight alternating bends where the robot runs wide, so a slower entry gives more time to correct. The oval finish time rises from about 1.86 s to roughly 2.0 s, still inside the 3.0 s limit, so completion should hold. The time term loses only a few points. (4) Keep kp 2.0 and ki 0.1, since the motor-mismatch correction is still useful.

Expected result: the oval completion rate stays at or near 0.85, with mean finish time about 2.0 s. s-bend and slalom progress should rise, and line-loss events and oscillation should fall. This is a single-variable test of speed, so the telemetry should show whether speed is what limits the bends. If the score does not move, the next step should test sensor weights or a larger kp change on the verified geometry.
